bib.title: DEBERTA: DECODING-ENHANCED BERT WITH DISENTANGLED ATTENTION

question: Can a BERT-style encoder with disentangled content/position attention and an enhanced mask decoder pretrain more efficiently and outperform RoBERTa and similar PLMs?
hypothesis: Attention weights depend on content and relative position, and absolute positions are better added late (before the softmax) than at the input, so both changes improve pre-training efficiency and downstream accuracy.
contributions: Disentangled attention with separate content and relative-position vectors
Enhanced mask decoder injecting absolute positions before the output softmax
Scale-invariant fine-tuning (SiFT), virtual adversarial training on normalised embeddings
1.5B-parameter model that surpasses the human baseline on SuperGLUE

method.summary: Encoder-only transformer pretrained with MLM using disentangled attention (c2c, c2p, p2c terms) and an enhanced mask decoder with absolute positions; fine-tuned with Adam, and SiFT for the 1.5B model. Evaluated on GLUE, SuperGLUE, SQuAD, RACE, ReCoRD, SWAG, NER, Wikitext-103.
method.task: masked language model pretraining and NLU fine-tuning

datasets.name: Pretraining corpus (base/large)
datasets.size: about 78GB after dedup (Wikipedia 12GB, BookCorpus 6GB, OpenWebText 38GB, Stories 31GB)
datasets.preprocessing: dedup (Shoeybi et al., 2019); BPE vocab of Radford et al. 2019 / Liu et al. 2019c

datasets.name: Pretraining corpus (1.5B)
datasets.source: Table 7 marks 4 sources; new 128K vocab built on it

datasets.name: SQuAD v1.1 / v2.0, RACE, ReCoRD, SWAG, CoNLL 2003
datasets.size: SQuAD1.1 87.6k, v2.0 130.3k, RACE 87,866, SWAG 73.5k, CoNLL 14,987 train

models.name: DeBERTa-1.5B
models.architecture: as above plus shared position/content projections, conv layer beside first layer, 128K vocab

models.name: RoBERTa, XLNet, ELECTRA, BERT, ALBERT, Megatron, T5

training.objective: MLM (15% masked, 10% unchanged, 10% random, rest [MASK]) with dynamic batching and span masking up to 3; RTD variant in A.11
training.optimizer: Adam with weight decay; eps 1e-6, beta1 0.9, beta2 0.999
training.tokens: inferred: 2 billion training samples (1M steps x 2K); token count not stated
training.seq_len: inferred: 512 from max relative distance k=512; not stated explicitly
training.regularisation: gradient clipping 1.0; SiFT only on 1.5B SuperGLUE
training.hardware: V100 on DGX-2: 16 nodes (1.5B), 6 nodes/96 GPUs (large), 4 nodes/64 GPUs (base), 1 node/16 GPUs (ablation)
training.seeds: fine-tuning: average of five runs with different seeds

other.EMD: 2 layers sharing weights, absolute position embedding as I

inference.samples: 5 fine-tuning runs with different seeds, averaged

other.generation: DeBERTa-MT uses triangular self-attention mask for ARLM

metrics.name: Accuracy / F1 / EM / Matthews corr / Pearson corr / perplexity

eval.protocol: Dev sets for most tasks, model selection on dev; average of five seeds with significance test (p<0.05); SuperGLUE test via server

results.quote: surpass the human performance on SuperGLUE for the ﬁrst time in terms of macro-average score (89.9 versus 89.8)

results.claim: Ensemble DeBERTa tops SuperGLUE leaderboard above the human baseline.
results.setup: DeBERTaEnsemble, SuperGLUE test, as of 6 Jan 2021
results.quote: outperforming the human baseline by a decent margin (90.3 versus 89.8)

limits: Authors concede the model is far from human-level NLU, lacking compositional generalization.
SiFT only applied to DeBERTa-1.5B on SuperGLUE; fuller study deferred.
Large-model comparisons confound data size and steps (78GB vs 160GB); controlled comparison only at base scale with Wikipedia+BookCorpus.
T5 comparison is on test results not comparable with dev results.
Several settings (precision, exact seq length, total compute, token count) are not stated.

terms.definition: incorporate absolute positions right after all the Transformer layers but before the softmax layer for masked token prediction
Scale-invariant-Fine-Tuning: perturbations applied to normalized word embeddings in virtual adversarial training

lineage.work: Shaw et al. relative position representations
